## Instructions

Complete this tutorial while reading Sections 9.5 - 9.7 of the [textbook](https://nustat.github.io/intro-stat-data-sci/09-sampling-distributions.html). Each question allows 3 'free' attempts. After the third attempt a 10% deduction occurs per attempt.

You can click the "View Grade" button as many times as you would like to see your current grade and the number of attempts you are on. Before submitting make sure your grade is as expected.

### Goals

-   Describe how differing sample sizes affect the sampling distribution.
-   Understand the Central Limit Theorem, its conditions, and how to use this theorem.

## Reading Quiz

```{r Q}
quiz(
  caption = NULL,
  # Q1 (9.5.1)
  question_blank("<strong> Q1) Consider the data frame `virtual_prop_red_100` that results from the following lines of code: </strong> <br/>
<pre><code>virtual_samples_100 &lt;- bowl %&gt;%
  rep_sample_n(size = 100, reps = 10000)
&nbsp;
virtual_prop_red_100 &lt;- virtual_samples_100 %&gt;%
  group_by(replicate) %&gt;%
  summarize(red = sum(color == 'red')) %&gt;%
  mutate(prop_red = red / 100)</code></pre><br/>a) How many rows will <code>virtual_prop_red_100</code> have? ___ <br/>b) What is the maximum possible value of the <code>red</code> column (even if it is highly unlikely)? ___ <br/>c) What is the maximum possible value of the <code>prop_red</code> column (even if it is highly unlikely)? ___ <br/>d) How many rows will have <code>replicate == 437</code>? ___",
           answer_fn(function(value){
                if (str_remove_all(value, "[\\s,]") == "10000") {
                    return(mark_as(TRUE))}
                    return(mark_as(FALSE)) }),
           answer("100", correct = TRUE),
           answer("1", correct = TRUE),
           answer("1", correct = TRUE),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q2 (NEW, 9.5.1)
  question_numeric("Q2) According to Table 9.7, what is the standard error of the proportion red when using the shovel with 25 slots? Round to 3 decimal places.",
           answer(0.098, correct = TRUE),
           step = 0.001,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q3 (9.5.1)
  question("Q3) Consider using shovels of size 200 and 75 to sample from the bowl of red and white balls. Which of the following are TRUE statements? Select all that apply.",
           answer("Using a shovel of size 200 would result in a larger standard error for proportions red, compared to using a shovel of size 75."),
           answer("Using a shovel of size 200 would result in there being more variation in estimates of proportion red, compared to using a shovel of size 75."),
           answer("Using a shovel of size 200 would give an estimate $\\widehat{\\pi}$ that is likely to be closer to the true population parameter $\\pi$, compared to using a shovel of size 75.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("Using a shovel of size 200 would result in the sampling distribution of $\\widehat{\\pi}$ having a smaller standard deviation, compared to using a shovel of size 75.", correct = TRUE),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q4 (NEW, 9.5.1)
  question("Q4) According to the reading, why is it a general mathematical property that increasing the sample size decreases the standard error?",
           answer("The sample size $n$ appears in some form in the denominator of each standard error formula.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("Larger samples always contain more extreme values."),
           answer("Larger samples make the estimator biased."),
           answer("The population parameter changes as the sample size increases."),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q5 (9.5)
  question_blank("<strong> Q5) Imagine that you have a random sample of students who took the SAT in Illinois, and you find the average SAT Math score in your sample to be $\\overline{x}$ = 527 and the standard deviation of SAT Math scores to be 100. </strong> <br/>
a) What is the standard error of your estimate $\\overline{x}$ if your sample has 100 students? ___ <br/>
b) What is the standard error of your estimate $\\overline{x}$ if your sample has 400 students? ___ <br/>
c) Which sample size (100 or 400) gives a more precise estimate? ___",
           answer_fn(function(value){
                if (str_trim(value) %in% c("10", "10.0")) {
                    return(mark_as(TRUE))}
                    return(mark_as(FALSE)) }),
           answer_fn(function(value){
                if (str_trim(value) %in% c("5", "5.0")) {
                    return(mark_as(TRUE))}
                    return(mark_as(FALSE)) }),
           answer_fn(function(value){
                if (str_trim(value) == "400") {
                    return(mark_as(TRUE))}
                    return(mark_as(FALSE)) }),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q6 (NEW, 9.6)
  question("Q6) According to the Central Limit Theorem, the sampling distribution of the sample mean $\\overline{x}$ is well approximated by:",
           answer("A Normal distribution with mean $\\mu$ and standard error $\\frac{\\sigma}{\\sqrt{n}}$", correct = TRUE),
           answer("A Normal distribution with mean $\\mu$ and standard error $\\sigma$"),
           answer("A chi-squared distribution with $n - 1$ degrees of freedom"),
           answer("The same distribution as the population, whatever its shape"),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q7 (NEW, 9.6.1)
  question("Q7) Which of the following are conditions for the Central Limit Theorem to apply? Select all that apply.",
           answer("Sampled observations must be independent, which is more likely with random sampling / assignment and a sample size less than 10% of the population.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("Either the population distribution is Normal, or, if it is skewed, the sample size is large.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("The population distribution must be Normal."),
           answer("The sample size must be greater than 1,000."),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q8 (NEW, 9.6.2)
  question("Q8) In the infant mortality example, the underlying data was skewed right. What happened to the sampling distribution of the mean as the sample size increased from $n = 5$ to $n = 30$?",
           answer("At $n = 5$ it was still slightly skewed right, but at $n = 30$ it was approximately Normal.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("It was approximately Normal at both $n = 5$ and $n = 30$."),
           answer("It stayed skewed right at both sample sizes, because the data was skewed right."),
           answer("It became wider as the sample size increased."),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q9 (9.6)
  question("Q9) Which of the following are TRUE statements about $\\overline{x}$? Select all that apply.",
           answer("In large enough samples, it will be Normally distributed, even if the underlying data is skewed.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("Its sampling distribution will become wider as sample size increases."),
           answer("Its standard error depends on the sample size.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("Its sampling distribution will be centered around the true population mean ($\\mu$).", correct = TRUE),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q10 (NEW, 9.7)
  question("Q10) Statisticians summarize a sampling distribution in three ways. Which of the following are among them? Select all that apply.",
           answer("Its shape / distribution (e.g. Normal)", correct = TRUE),
           answer("Its average value compared to the population parameter (bias)", correct = TRUE),
           answer("Its standard deviation (standard error)", correct = TRUE),
           answer("Its sample size"),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q11 (9.7)
  question("Q11) Which of the following are TRUE about the theory of repeated samples? Select all that apply.",
           answer("It is a purely theoretical construct - you will not observe repeated samples in real life.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("It provides the theory for how we can connect a sample estimate to the population parameter we care about.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("It relies on the process of randomization (e.g. random sampling).", correct = TRUE),
           answer("It ensures that we will get a precise estimate of the population parameter."),
           answer("It helps us to determine if an estimator (e.g. $\\overline{x}$ or $s^2$) is unbiased.", correct = TRUE),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE)
)
```
